english.title: Fail to comply with requirements concerning statement of affairs where liquidator appointed
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a person required by the official receiver in accordance with section 131(1) of the Insolvency Act 1986 to make out and submit to

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

a statement in the prescribed form and verified by a statement of truth as to the affairs of **(..SPECIFY COMPANY..), a company in respect of which

(C)_[a winding up order had been made,]_
(D)_[a provisional liquidator had been appointed,]_

before **(..SPECIFY DEADLINE DATE..) being the end of the

(E)_[period of 21 days beginning with the day after that on which the prescribed notice of the requirement was given to you by the official receiver,]_
(F)_[extended period given by the official receiver under section 131(5)(b) of the Act,]_

failed, without reasonable excuse, to do so
english.legislation: Contrary to section 131(7) of, and schedule 10 to, the Insolvency Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
fail without reasonable excuse
to comply with a s. 131 obligation

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum or a fine not exceeding one-tenth of the statutory maximum for each day on which the act or the failure continues.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
